text:
anya: Quick heads-up — merchant finetune merge for customer 'Merchantly' surfaced a tokenization mismatch in our quick-eval pack. Outputs are getting truncated mid-sentence for templates that start with special tokens.

mike: details? raw numbers?

anya: summary below, ran the 30-case smoke pack on int4 + adapter-merge. Most passes but two failure clusters: answer cutoff and hallucinated currency conversion.

sara: :eyes: can you paste the merge command and checkpoint ids?

anya: sure:
```
# merge base + adapter
redwood merge --base gpt-open-7b --adapter merchantly_lora_v1 --out merged/merchantly-v1
redwood quantize --input merged/merchantly-v1 --bits 4 --out merged/merchantly-v1-int4
```

anya: quick eval summary (30 cases):
- EM: 88.3%
- BLEU-like: 75.2
- Rouge-L: 81.1
- Perplexity (subset): base 6.2 -> merged-int4 7.0
- Failures: 2/30 (both truncation at token boundary), 3/30 minor formatting misaligns

mike: truncation at token boundary sounds like tokenizer id shift. Did adapter alter special token embeddings or add new tokens?

anya: adapter was a LoRA on top of same vocab, but during exporter we used a different tokenizer mapping script (token_map_v2) to remap new presentation tokens for that customer's templates. suspect off-by-one in mapping for <CURRENCY> token.

kevin: can you paste the offending input and model output for one failing case?

anya: example:
```
INPUT: <INVOICE><CURRENCY> Convert 100.
EXPECTED: $100.00
MODEL OUT: $100.00
<INVOICE> Thank you for your order.
```
actual output got cut: "$100.00" and then stopped mid-sentence in other cases.

sara: hmm the example looks fine, but another failing case produced: "€ 42.50\uFFFDD" — weird unicode marker.

pipeline-bot: CI: eval-pack-runner completed for thread 1762223334 — 30 tests, 2 failures, logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/rs/1762223334

mike: @kevin any known issues with token_map_v2? I remember a bug where new special tokens were appended but indices not patched in the kv-cache offset logic.

kevin: yep there was a hotfix for kv-offsets back in 1740000000 series. If tokenizer mapping shifts indices, the kv cache offset math in the runtime can mis-align past the first special token leading to premature EOS detection. I'll reproduce locally.

anya: repro steps I used attached in CI logs. Also noted that patched adapter merges where adapter added a pseudo-token for merchant names can shift indices by +1.

kevin: plan: I'll try two approaches in parallel:
1) re-export with token_map_v1 (legacy mapping) and re-run pack
2) keep token_map_v2 but apply kv-offset patch in runtime and smoke test

sara: good. prioritize approach (1) for customer safety, approach (2) for long-term fix.

anya: agreed. I'll re-run with v1 and post results. tagging @mike for customer update draft after we confirm.

mike: thanks. pls ping once v1 results are in. If v1 fixes it we'll schedule a hotfix release for the merged checkpoint and update the onboarding checklist.

kevin: started local repro, will push branch `kv-offset-fix/merchantly` if I can confirm.

anya: thanks everyone. I'll update thread with new eval pack result (rerun expected in ~20m).

(20m later)

anya: rerun with token_map_v1 -> 30/30 green, no truncations. Confirmed mapping was culprit. Posting diff in next message.

anya: diff (excerpt):
```
- special tokens mapping: <CURRENCY> -> 50256
+ special tokens mapping: <CURRENCY> -> 50255
```

mike: great. let's roll v1 merged-int4 to staging and notify customer that we found token-map mismatch. Follow-up: kevin to land runtime guard so future exports don't break.

kevin: will open PR for kv-offset-guard and add unit that fuzzes special token insertions into kv indexing.

sara: add a short checklist item under eng-ml/adapters: "verify token_map version + kv-offset sanity".

anya: done. created internal doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/adapter-tokenmap-guidance

mike: awesome. closing loop. :white_check_mark:
